name: ESP32-C3 SuperMini
description: The default $2-3 ESP32-C3 board: 22.5 x 18 mm, USB-C, 4 MB flash, 13 GPIOs, BLE 5 and Wi-Fi; unbeatable on price, but with a weak ceramic antenna.
notes: Pin order with USB-C at the top: left column GPIO5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 20 (RX), 21 (TX); right column 5V, GND, 3V3, GPIO4, 3, 2, 1, 0. Row spacing is not published, so no carrier-board header data is provided.
ESP32-C3FH4 with 4 MB in-package flash. No UART bridge: native USB CDC/JTAG, so enable 'USB CDC On Boot' in Arduino; hold BOOT while plugging in if it is not detected.
Blue user LED on GPIO8 (shared with I2C SDA), red power LED. GPIO2, 8 and 9 are strapping pins (GPIO9 is the BOOT button).
The tiny ceramic antenna is the most common complaint (poor range, some batches badly tuned); a quarter-wave wire mod helps a lot.
Multiple look-alike clone batches exist with identical pinout; no official vendor page.
